name: Loopy
rules: Draw one closed loop along the grid lines. It never crosses or branches, so every dot has two lines or none. A number says how many of its four sides the loop uses; cells with no number are free.
technique.1: This number already has all the lines it needs around it, so its other sides are crosses.
technique.2: This number has exactly as many open sides left as lines it still needs, so all of them are lines.
technique.3: A line comes into a corner of this number from outside, so the two sides meeting at that corner can't both be lines, and every other open side of the number must be a line.
technique.4: No line reaches this dot and only one of its sides is still open. One line alone at a dot is a dead end, so cross that side off.
technique.5: A line reaches this dot and only one of its other sides is still open. A dot can never have just one line, so the loop continues along that side.
technique.6: This dot already has its two lines, so cross off its remaining sides.
technique.7: The lines forced at the corners of this number already give it all the lines it needs, so this side is a cross.
technique.8: Even with every line still possible at its corners, this number falls short without this side, so this side is a line.
technique.9: Drawing this segment would close a loop that leaves other lines out, so it is a cross.
technique.10: The loop is complete and every number is satisfied, so every remaining segment is a cross.
demo.1: Draw one closed loop along the grid lines. A number counts the lines on that cell's four sides; a blank cell is free.
demo.2: Start with a 0. None of its four sides can be a line, so cross them off.
demo.4: A line that stops dead is not a loop. Every dot needs two lines, or none at all.
demo.5: It cannot branch either. Three lines at a dot is too many.
demo.6: One closed circuit, and every number matched. Follow it round and you arrive back where you started.
